name: Phenethylphenylacetoxypiperidine
summary: PEPAP (phenethylphenylacetoxypiperidine) is an opioid analgesic that is an analog of desmethylprodine. It is related to the drug MPPP, with an N-phenethyl group in place of the N-methyl substitution and an acetate ester rather than propionate. PEPAP is approximately 6–7 times more potent than morphine in laboratory rats.

pharmacology.text: PEPAP has been found to be a potent CYP2D6 inhibitor, which makes it likely to cause adverse interactions with some other drugs, although the inhibitory potency of PEPAP is less than that of MPPP. In animal experiments, only MPTP analogues that preserved the N-methyl-4-phenyl-1,2,3,6-tetrahydropyridine structure were active as dopaminergic neurotoxins.

sideEffects.text: Side effects can include itching, nausea and potentially serious respiratory depression which can be life-threatening.

uses.en: It is a research compound with no medical use.
uses.zh: 它是研究用化合物，沒有醫療用途。
uses.zhHans: 它是研究用化合物，没有医疗用途。

fact.en: Its close relative MPPP is infamous: badly made batches sold in California in 1982 contained the contaminant MPTP, which destroyed dopamine cells and left several young people with sudden, permanent parkinsonism.
fact.zh: 它的近親 MPPP 相當惡名昭彰：1982 年在加州販售的劣質批次含有污染物 MPTP，它會破壞多巴胺細胞，使數名年輕人突然出現永久性的帕金森症狀。
fact.zhHans: 它的近亲 MPPP 相当恶名昭彰：1982 年在加州贩售的劣质批量含有污染物 MPTP，它会破坏多巴胺细胞，使数名年轻人突然出现永久性的帕金森症状。
